packageRules.description: Major bumps for OOXML/DOCX libs require manual review — may change numbering or content control behavior

Node pin (ADR-081): only propose npm releases whose own engines.node overlaps ours. The constraint itself is auto-detected from engines.node and .nvmrc — deliberately NOT declared in a `constraints` block, because Renovate treats a manually-set constraint as fixed and will never offer to bump it, which would fork the source of truth. Scoped to runtime dependencies per Renovate's guidance that strict filtering across devDependencies filters far more than most users expect.

Node pin (ADR-081): never propose a Node MAJOR bump. Moving LTS majors is a deliberate coordinated change across .nvmrc, both engines.node ranges, both @types/node majors and CI — not a routine dependency PR. Minor/patch within the pinned major stays enabled.
Node pin (ADR-081): keep .nvmrc and any workflow node-version on the pinned major. Bounded rather than disabled outright so security patches inside 24.x still flow.

Node pin (ADR-081): @types/node must track the runtime major. A typings-only bump past the runtime lets tsc accept APIs that do not exist at execution — exactly what PR #557 proposed (@types/node 26 against a Node 22 runtime) and why it was closed.

Toolchain pin: stay on TypeScript 5.x. TS 6.0 (2026-03-23) and 7.0 postdate the training cutoffs of the models doing implementation work here (Sonnet 5 / Fable 5: Jan 2026), so a compiler they cannot write against reliably is a poor trade for capability this project does not need. Declined three times (#565, #560, #593/#597/#598) — bounded so it stops being re-proposed weekly. Lift deliberately, moving root and tools/verify together.

Toolchain pin: stay on ESLint 9.x. ESLint 10 (2026-02-06) postdates the same model cutoffs, and the flat config here is agent-edited often enough that the cost is real. Declined in #573/#559 — bounded so it stops recurring. Lift deliberately, moving root and tools/verify together.

Database pin: stay on Postgres 18 (EOL 2030-11-14). The earlier block on 18 was a misdiagnosis — SQLSTATE reaches the driver fine; Postgres 18 reports an ON DELETE RESTRICT rejection as the SQL-standard restrict_violation (23001) instead of the generic foreign_key_violation (23503), which the error map did not recognise. Resolved in #599 (ADR-084) by accepting both codes. Bounded rather than unpinned so 18.x patches flow while a future major stays a deliberate, tested move — same shape as the node (<25), typescript (<6.0.0) and eslint (<10.0.0) bounds.
